# Rear differential breather extension

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Extend the rear differential breather by routing a rubber hose through the frame to catch rainwater. [t1271]

[Partial] Remove the existing rear differential vent hose to thread a barbed nipple directly into the axle housing. [t1271]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Locate the stock breather assembly under the rig.
2. Slit the end of the rubber hose with a razor blade to fit it onto the nipple.
3. [Partial] Bust off or unscrew the old brass nipple from the diff case using a 13mm wrench if necessary.
4. Reach over the frame cross member and remove the screw holding the breather assembly with a 10mm wrench.
5. Remove the tail light by taking out two Phillips head screws and pulling it straight back.
6. Tape off one end of an eight-foot length of quarter-inch diameter rubber hose to keep dirt out.
7. Insert the taped end of the hose into the frame hole located just behind the cross member.
8. Push the hose through until a large section protrudes from the rear near the shackle.
9. Thread the loose end of the tube up through the vertical hole at the rail's tip and towards the bumperette.
10. [Partial] Squeeze the hose between the bumperette assembly and the tail lamp housing to secure it in place.
11. Cut off any excess plastic nub on the protruding section of the frame using a saw blade or rotary tool.
12. Drill a three-eighths inch hole through the flange sticking out from that cut-off piece.
13. Thread the hose end through this new drilled hole and point it toward the shelf to catch rainwater.
14. Secure the hose above the axle with zip ties so it rests away from hot exhaust pipes at full droop.

_Procedure reported by [t1271]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-extend-your-rear-diff-breather.2628/>_

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1271] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Remove the existing rear differential vent hose.
2. [Partial] Thread a barbed nipple fitting directly into the axle housing.

</details>

## Tools

- 10mm wrench [t1271]
- [Partial] Razor blade or saw blade [t1271]

- Drill with 3/8-bit [t1271]

## Parts

- Barbed nipple: Nissan part number 38323-C601A or similar [t1271]
- [Partial] Fuel line hose: Approximately 7 to 8 feet long with 3/16 inch inner diameter [t1271]
- [Partial] Hose clamp: Small size for securing hose [t1271]
- Nipple fitting: Brass or steel, 1/8 NPT female thread [t1271]
- [Partial] Rubber hose: 1/4 inch ID, 3/8 OD fuel line or similar [t1271]

## Specifications

- **New flange hole diameter**: 3/8 inch [t1271] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Stock breather nipple thread pitch**: 1/8 NPT [t1271] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- Use a 10mm wrench to reach the screw on the breather assembly from over the frame. [t1271]
- Choose hose designed for petroleum products like fuel line to withstand gear oil fumes and weathering. [t1271]
- [Partial] Select a wall thickness of 3/8 OD if available, as it is closer to stock than common 1/2 OD options. [t1271]
- [Partial] Turn the vent hose back down and add a filter at the top of the tail light opening for better placement. [t1271]
- Use epoxy on the nipple fitting if standard tolerances are tight, then secure it tightly. [t1271]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Over-stressing the thin walls of the original nipple when removing the hose without slitting it first. [t1271]
